messages:
elena - customer-success: Heads-up — Acme (acct: acme-prod) just escalated. They hit a production crash when using our JSON/structured_output mode: client lib fails to parse, raising a 422 on their side. They say it started after a model upgrade last night. stack trace attached to ticket #INC-3421 :grimacing:

maria - support: Can you paste the raw model response they received? Also need the request trace id or example request ts so we can join logs/trace.

elena - customer-success: Pasted below (redacted emails/tokens). They included the full body from our API response body: 
```
{
  "items": [
    {"id": 1, "name": "widget", "qty": 3},
    {"id": 2, "name": "gadget", "qty": 5},
  ],
  "summary": {"total": 8}
}
```
They said the trailing comma on the second array element crashes their strict JSON parser. Customer's SDK is strict and throws before their validation layer.

maria - support: That looks like a model-formatting issue — trailing comma and sometimes we see extra commentary after JSON (e.g. "\n\nNote: prices estimated"). Do we have a telemetry metric for structured output parse failures?

lex - eng-sre: Not today in the default dashboards. We log raw model output in the inference trace (redacted) with trace_id. But we do not currently count parse failures as a distinct metric. We can add a log-based metric that increments when output fails our JSON-mode sanitizer/parsing check. Suggest name: structured_output.parse_failure.count tagged by model, model_version, deployment_zone, customer_id (redact in UI).

sanjay - eng-ml: Repro steps from Acme in their report: 
1) POST /v1/generate with header `Accept: application/json` and body includes `mode: "json"` and the schema prompt attached. 
2) model: open-llama-65b-quant v2.1, temperature=0.0, max_tokens=256, streaming=false
3) sample prompt (redacted) that asks for an array of items and a summary.
Repro on our side: calling same model on dedicated staging returned valid JSON 8/10 runs, invalid JSON 2/10 (non-deterministic).

maria - support: Customer also reported latency spikes during failures — ~800ms -> 3.2s for those requests, and they saw duplicate billing events on their side (they retry). Need to confirm if the SDK retries on 5xx only or also on client-side parse errors.

lex - eng-sre: Important: correlate traces for the slow requests. I pulled two trace_ids that match INC-3421: trace_xX1 and trace_xX2. I see increased tokenization time and a model-side streaming rebuffer event in the logs. Might be a kernel fallback on quantized kernels that emits extra whitespace/newline tokens at the end of the response.

elena - customer-success: They asked for a hotfix or workaround. What can we offer quickly?

sanjay - eng-ml: Short-term: recommend the customer switch to tolerant parsing (json5-ish) or strip trailing commas before parsing. Offer a small snippet they can drop in their client: 
```js
// tolerant cleanup before JSON.parse
const cleaned = responseText.replace(/,\s*([}\]])/g, '$1').trim();
const obj = JSON.parse(cleaned);
```
Longer-term: we should add a sanitizer step in the platform for JSON-mode outputs that enforces strict-schema conformant output and returns a structured failure code with trace_id when model output fails validation. That lets clients detect and retry safely without double-billing.

maria - support: For now I've given Acme the cleanup snippet + advise to set client retry to only 5xx and 429, not on parse errors. Also suggested they use streaming=true in dev to see partial output. They want visibility into occurrences.

lex - eng-sre: Action items: 
- Add a log-based metric (structured_output.parse_failure.count) + Grafana panel showing rate per model and per customer (redacted ids).
- Create an alert: >0.5% parse_fail rate over 5m for any customer -> P1.
- Emit a structured failure event in traces and in audit logs with `failure_type=JSON_PARSE` and `trace_id` and `model_version`. Make sure we redact user PII (emails, api keys) before storing.

sanjay - eng-ml: Also to reduce root cause: we can pin model kernel config to avoid the fallback behavior for dedicated customers or apply a post-generation cleanup pass that strips trailing commas/newlines and validates against the requested schema. Rolling that out to hosted customers may need opt-in initially.

elena - customer-success: Customer asked for a temporary mitigation on their account: route to a fallback model variant (open-llama-65b-quant v2.0) that has historically lower parse failures. Can we do that per-customer routing?

lex - eng-sre: Yes, we already support request-routing by customer via a routing policy. Ops: I can add a policy to pin acme-prod to v2.0 for the next 24h. Setting it now. :rocket:

ops-bot: Routing policy updated for customer=acme-prod -> model=open-llama-65b-quant@v2.0 (effective immediately)

maria - support: Follow-up plan I told Acme: 1) apply client-side tolerant parse + no-retry on parse errors, 2) we'll pin them to v2.0 for 24h, 3) we will notify when we deploy a sanitizer and metric + dashboard, 4) we will share trace_ids for any future failures to correlate.

lex - eng-sre: I'll open ENG-OBS ticket to add metric + dashboard + alert (ENG-OBS-789). Will include the query for logs: 
```
query: status:inference AND context.mode:json AND parse_status:failure | stats count() by model_version, customer_id
```
Mask customer_id in the dashboard with hashed IDs.

sanjay - eng-ml: I'll add a post-processing validation hook in the runtime to do schema validation and sanitize common trailing-comma/extra-text errors. If validation fails, runtime returns 422 with body `{ "error": "STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_INVALID", "trace_id": "<id>" }` and logs sanitized sample for debug (pii-redacted).

elena - customer-success: Perfect — please notify me when ENG-OBS-789 and the runtime hook PRs are merged. I'll update the customer and close INC-3421 once they confirm stability.

maria - support: Added internal note to INC-3421 with all action items and pinned the workaround snippet. Marking follow-up tasks to check billing telemetry for retried requests. :white_check_mark:

lex - eng-sre: One more note on observability & redaction: ensure raw output is stored only in short-term hot logs (7d) and scrubbed for emails/api-keys, then move to long-term aggregated metrics. We should never store raw user-prompt or unredacted outputs beyond debugging TTL.

elena - customer-success: Thanks team — keeping this thread open until runtime hook + dashboard are live. :pray:

maria - support: Assigning owners: lex for dashboards/alerts, sanjay for runtime sanitizer, elena to own the customer comms.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from lex, :pray: from elena)
